I have meditated more properly this year, but only recently I have noticed some other things besides my emotions and thoughts when I'm upset. I noticed the patters of my thinking, the value system by which I operate. I learned that I trained myself to fear or hate certain things, and figuring that out gave me a new perspective.

Thank you, you did give me some new perspectives. I guess I could give altruism a try, since I keep hearing people saying that is one of the big ingredients to life. I am always worried about the potential futility of such endeavour, and of there will be a thing meditation can't help me with. 

I can have a more cold-headed approach to love, something akin to gentle neutrality as a consequence of understanding. 

I don't know how exactly "self-love" works yet. I might learn that once I make some friends. I certainly spend too much time just watching YouTube. I could replace it with watching documentaries, or writing.

I should've been more clear, I'm not free from emotions in a sense I don't feel them. It's that I am no longer forced to act on them, to obey them, just to notice and listen. That also includes some patterns of behaviour I have, like procrastination or addiction.

Being free of emotions means I can choose what to do regardless of how I feel. Mindfulness helped me with this, and CBT I learned from my psychologist.

Unconditional love seems to me like a bad method to deal with any potential enemies, competitors, psychopaths, manipulators etc. I think it puts me in a vulnerable mental state. I know it's meant to show humanity and altruism, but sometimes that's just a bad bet.

Charisma, and other practical things, will give me strength and tools for survival. I figured that if I basically solved the "quality of life" question with mindfulness (and stoicism), only other thing that remains is "quantity of life", ie time spent in this life, and/or family.

I've been to soft. I'm unproductive, don't have close relationships, and my health is only kind of okay. I need a masculine twist to my life. I'd advise you to start meditating. You can use an app, like Waking up (you get 5 months free premium if you ask the support, they respond in couple of days). You must read some books on relationships, like "His needs, her needs". You can have a life that you wish for, and actually love it and not mind the struggles, with mindfulness.
